generated_note: SOURCE OF TRUTH. The API validates against this, the web renders from it, and the agent compiles its speech grammar from it. Run scripts/contracts.ps1 after editing. Never hand-edit the generated copies.
game_note: Rebuilt from the owner's in-game menu list. A category is a place to look, an item is the request, and everything else is a tag on it. The game has far more distinct things than a request type each, and a tag is what a board row can show and a shopping list can group.

roles.game_note: FOB-built mortars. Fires on a Shell request.
SPH-2 self-propelled gun. Fires on a Shell request.
Fire delivered from the air. Rotary today; a fixed-wing airframe would be the same job, so the role names the effect and not the airframe.
Can engage aircraft. A Stingray crew, an infantryman with an AA launcher, anyone who can reach air. Never a piece of equipment.
Can kill armour. Infantry launchers, a tank crew, a crewed emplacement. Held alongside another role, not instead of one.
Rifleman. Fireteam work, smoke screens, and the requester for most mobility.
Overwatch: counter-sniper and cover. Replaced recon, which nothing targeted.
Revives and heals. Targeted by Infantry > Medical.
Trucks. Half of the delivery pair, and ground mobility.
Transport choppers. The other half of the delivery pair, plus paradrop and air extraction.
Keeps vehicles running: repair, refuel, rearm. Split back out of builder, which had absorbed it in the v3 rebuild and made every vehicle job fan out to all six crewed roles.
FOBs, defenses, emplacements and drills. Structures only: keeping a VEHICLE running is engineer.
The lead. No request targets it: it is who may restart a match and hand out roles, which is why it is grant_only and off the join default.

default_enabled_roles_note: Roles a group has on by default. The join default is every ENABLED role EXCEPT those marked grant_only, so a member who joins with no role_ids never lands on the command board. command is deliberately absent from this list as well as grant-gated: a role that is enabled but grant_only is still a role an admin can hand out without a group setting change.
menu_note: The request menu tree in 06-overlay-ux.md is GENERATED from these paths, not hand-drawn. A path is category.slot, or category.slot.slot for the third level under build. A type may appear at more than one leaf on purpose: EXTRACT sits under AIR, MOVE and MEDICAL because somebody under fire should find it down whichever branch they guessed first, and a duplicate entry costs one line of a static menu. Two DIFFERENT types may never share a leaf, which scripts/contracts.ps1 enforces.
structure_kinds_note: Empty. Build items are request types with their own tags now, because Defenses and Emplacement each carry a different option set and a structure kind cannot.

request_types.game_note: Bulk crates. The kind is carried in supply_kind, not in the type.
request_types.kind_note: A delivery MUST name what to bring, or the provider who accepts it cannot act on it. The default is building supplies, the commonest crate, so an unqualified "resupply" is a useful guess rather than an expensive one.
request_types.multi_taker_note: null: resolved from the chosen supply kind at submit.
request_types.ttl_note: 120 while it waits for a driver. A crate the kind marks multi_taker still waits 120: the kind decides who may take it, not how long it sits.

request_types.game_note: Any effect on a position or building. Replaces shell_mission, armor_support, close_air and fire_team: the requester names the target, not the deliverer.
request_types.solution_note: The bracket is a tool for whoever is shooting indirect. A row taken by a helicopter simply ignores it.

request_types.game_note: Replaces anti_armor_fire and the armour half of armor_support.
Replaces overwatch. Sniper is one of several answers, not the only one.
Replaces air_move and ground_move. Air or ground, whoever is up.
Air only. paradrop and hot are both outside the pronunciation subset, so the spoken form is air drop.

quantity_note: takes_quantity names the thing the count counts. It is NOT a modifier. Count used to be stuffed into modifiers text[], which made a partially delivered request unrepresentable: a driver asked for four runs who delivered two could only lie with 'done' or leave the row open, and two drivers could not split one request. It is now quantity_requested and quantity_delivered on Request, and the done verb carries a delivered count. A short completion re-opens the remainder under the SAME ticket rather than creating a second one. The numeral is still spoken in the modifier position class ('lift 6', 'resupply 4 pallets'); only its storage moved. A count belongs to a type only where the number IS the ask. Owner's call: move_transport keeps 'passengers' and nothing else does. attack_position lost 'rounds' (six target roles, and a fireteam cannot send three rounds to a position), resupply lost 'pallets' and build_builders lost 'bodies'. Do not add takes_quantity to a new type without asking. A type with no takes_quantity has no quantity, and quantity is never inferred from a modifier.

command_verbs.note: Claiming a request starts it. There is no separate start verb: the aliases that used to belong to one ('start', 'on it', 'moving', 'en route', 'working') all mean the same act.
The only terminal completion verb. Carries an outcome (serviced, no_longer_required, unable) on the completed event and an optional delivered count on a type with takes_quantity.
command_verbs.alias_note: 'splash' and 'rounds out' were aliases here and were WRONG. Both mean the rounds are in the air, which is exactly when the adjust loop should begin, so the most natural word in a gunner's vocabulary closed the mission before the spotter could speak and the requester's strip read ROUNDS OUT as completion. They now belong to rounds_away.

command_verbs.note: NON-TERMINAL. Writes the rounds_away RequestEvent and leaves state at in_progress so the spotter can still adjust. Also supplies the requester's ETA for free, because time of flight is already computed locally.
command_verbs.alias_note: 'shot' sits one feature above the floor against the adjust direction 'short' (AA1 versus AO1, S versus SH, T versus R-T: three of four). They are in DIFFERENT position classes, which is what makes the pair safe, and the cost of a swap is bounded because neither verb is terminal. Re-run the floor before either word moves class. 'on the way' shares its onset with the start alias 'on it'; longest_match_wins resolves it, and both readings are non-terminal. 'rounds out' as a first token does not collide with the 'rounds' quantity unit or the ammo supply alias, because those live in the modifier and kind classes.

command_verbs.note: NON-TERMINAL, spotter side. Spoken by whoever holds the paired spotter request, or by the requester. The matched alias IS the direction on the adjusted event payload; a trailing numeral supplies optional metres. 'adjust 3 over 50'.
command_verbs.alias_note: These four words are NOT initial-class tokens, and that is load-bearing rather than tidy. Bare 'left' is L EH1 F T against the incumbent 'lift' L IH1 F T: same syllable count, same onset, same coda, differing only in stressed vowel. One feature of four, REFUSED. Bare 'right' is R AY1 T against the incumbent 'ride' R AY1 D: same syllable count, same stressed vowel, same onset, differing only in coda voicing. One feature of four, REFUSED. Both would have routed a fire correction into a transport request. Confining them to the adjust_direction class, reachable only after 'adjust' or 'correction' plus a slot ref, removes the collision outright instead of papering it, and the four directions clear the floor comfortably against each other.

command_verbs.note: Six digits. Redeems a deployment invite. Valid with no memberships at all.
'role mortar' toggles that subscription on or off. 'roles' alone reads back the current set.
Shows the command card on the overlay. The only discovery path a visitor has.
Hides every request from that requester on this viewer's board for the rest of the match.
Puts that row's coordinate on the clipboard for pasting into game chat. Writes only; never synthesises the paste keystroke.
Sets your gun position at the cursor for fire solutions.
Reads back azimuth, elevation and time of flight for that row.
Opens the MATCH panel. Parity verb: MORE 3 on the keyboard.
Opens the PEOPLE panel. Parity verb: MORE 4 on the keyboard.
Opens the RANGE calculator. Parity verb: MORE 5, and TOOLS on the keyboard.
Opens the account link prompt. Parity verb: MORE 8. Two words: bare 'link' is one syllable with nothing to distinguish it.
Copies the invite code to the clipboard, as pressing it on the MATCH panel does.
Reads the coordinate off the screen, the same act the menu's read entry performs. Never 'read coords': 'coords' is outside the small model's lexicon and is silently dropped.
Cycles the overlay board full, dim, off. Parity verb for the RightAlt+B chord, which is the one control with no menu entry at all.
Opens the REQUEST surface. Parity verb for the UP key, which the overlay names REQUEST at rest. It was the one word on the resting hint that could not be said.
Opens the TOOLS surface. Parity verb for the TOOLS key. RANGE already had a verb; the surface holding it did not.
Steps the range calculator to the next weapon, as the cycle key does on that page.
Clears the stored gun position. 'clear' alone already means clear mutes, so this one is two words.

coordinate_handoff_moved: Lives in contracts/game-profile.json. The chat text format is a fact about the game, not about our request vocabulary.

position_classes.note: The recognizer only ever chooses among tokens legal at the current position. Collisions are computed PER CLASS, never across the whole vocabulary. This is why 'wall' and 'all' are perfect homophones and not a collision.
position_classes.initial: Request type aliases, command verbs, join, role, help. First token only. A verb declaring position_class puts its ALIASES elsewhere and enters through its entry_aliases, which are initial.
position_classes.modifier: Modifiers and counts. Only after a request type. A takes_quantity numeral is spoken here.
position_classes.kind: Supply kinds and structure kinds. Only after a type that takes one.
position_classes.slot: 1-9, next, top, all. Only after a command verb.
position_classes.adjust_direction: over, short, left, right. Only after the adjust verb and its slot ref. Kept out of the initial class because 'left' and 'right' both fall below the floor there, against 'lift' and 'ride'.
position_classes.digit: 0-9. Only after join, and exactly six of them.

phonetic_floor.note: Not a warning and not a later test. Two aliases in the same position class that fall below the floor stop the contract building.
phonetic_floor.rule: Two aliases in the same position class must differ in syllable count, OR in stressed vowel, OR in both onset and coda.

pronunciation_overrides.willy pete: W IH1 L IY0 P IY1 T
pronunciation_overrides.fpv: EH2 F P IY2 V IY1
pronunciation_overrides.medevac: M EH1 D IH0 V AE2 K
pronunciation_overrides.rounds out: R AW1 N D Z AW1 T
pronunciation_overrides.on the way: AA1 N DH AH0 W EY1

phonetic_floor.worked_example: lmg is EH2 L EH2 M JH IY1 and smg is EH2 S EH2 M JH IY1. Same syllable count, same stressed vowel IY1, same JH-IY coda, differing only in the onset of the first letter. One feature of four. REFUSED, which is why weapon_lmg says "machine gun" and weapon_smg says "sub gun". Nobody spells a weapon class out loud under fire anyway.
phonetic_floor.worked_example_2: left is L EH1 F T and lift is L IH1 F T. One syllable each, same L onset, same F-T coda, differing only in the stressed vowel. One feature of four. REFUSED in the initial class, which is why the adjust directions live in their own position class instead. right versus ride fails the same way on coda voicing alone.
phonetic_floor.cross_class_note: The floor is computed PER POSITION CLASS. Moving a token to a class where its rival cannot appear is a legitimate fix and is not the same as suppressing the check: the recognizer genuinely never chooses between them. Moving a token to dodge a floor failure without checking it against its NEW class is the way to reintroduce the bug somewhere else.

ambiguous_aliases_note: An alias listed under a type's ambiguous_aliases is recognised but NEVER resolved by confidence. When it is the top hypothesis and a competing type is within the margin, the agent shows a two-item menu instead of guessing. It costs one keypress in the rare case and makes a confidently wrong request impossible. The generator also adds any pair it finds within 1.25x the floor.
grammar_rules_note: slot_quarantine_s was DELETED, not retuned. Nine slots with a 20 s quarantine admitted at most nine rows per 20 s no matter how fast providers cleared them, capping the board at 0.45 rows per second while overflow grew. Allocation is now least-recently-released: a digit is never reissued until all eight others have been, which is strictly better collision protection than a 20 s hold at zero dead time. ttl_s is a flat 120 s on every type: it is how long a request waits for a taker, not how long the job stays useful, and an unclaimed row that nobody wanted in two minutes is re-requested rather than left to rot. A claimed row does not expire at all. low_priority_slot_residency_s demotes a low-priority row to overflow after 60 s while leaving it OPEN, so it yields its digit at the halfway mark rather than holding one for its whole life; it must stay strictly below ttl_s or demotion never fires. coalesce_radius_units and coalesce_window_s are the submit-time dedup window: same type, same deployment, a point inside 0.50 units, created inside 60 s, attaches the new participant as a co-requester and returns the existing request. The quantity qualifier renders it as MORTAR x5. Same participant supersedes instead of coalescing.

forbidden_aliases.air support: Shares an unstressed distinguishing syllable with 'air transport'. Use 'close air'.
forbidden_aliases.smoke: Already a modifier on attack_position and the tactical kit. For a screening mission use 'screen'.
forbidden_aliases.fuel: Already a supply kind on resupply. For one stranded vehicle use 'refuel'.
forbidden_aliases.a t: Letter names are the worst case for the recognizer and it collides with 'eight'. Use 'anti tank'.
forbidden_aliases.support: Ambiguous across air_support, the two transports and the Wardogs Support track. Name the effect instead.
forbidden_aliases.left: FORBIDDEN in the initial class. One feature from 'lift' (same syllables, same L onset, same F-T coda). It is legal in adjust_direction, where 'lift' cannot appear.
forbidden_aliases.right: FORBIDDEN in the initial class. One feature from 'ride' (same syllables, same AY1, same R onset, coda differing only in voicing). It is legal in adjust_direction, where 'ride' cannot appear.
forbidden_aliases.rover: Never add it. One feature from the adjust direction 'over': same syllable count, same OW1, same coda, differing only in a null versus R onset. If a ground-vehicle type ever wants this word it must take a two-word form.

color_groups_note: A colour group answers what the role DOES, so a queue glyph reads without its label: fire, recon, move, build, medic, command. It is not the domain the role sits in.
icon_note: Two SVG path `d` strings on a 24x24 viewBox, stroke only, no fill. d2 may be empty. Served, never compiled in, so a glyph can be corrected without shipping a client.
menu_branch_labels_note: A label for a branch that holds items rather than being one. Without it a branch draws the label of whichever item landed on it first.
modifiers_note: The word a tag draws as. ModifierLabels derives one mechanically from the id when this has no entry, which mangles every real name in this game: t21 reads "T 21" and box_mags reads "BOX MAGS". Anything a person reads on a board row belongs here.
claim_grouping_note: Types sharing a group_key are ONE errand when they are at the same grid. Accepting one takes the others too, up to claim_group_max_extra, inside claim_group_radius_units. A squad needing a rifle, ammunition and a medkit at the same building files three requests because they are three different things, and the driver who takes one is driving to all three: without this the other two sit open behind somebody already standing there. The radius is wider than the coalesce radius on purpose. Coalescing merges the SAME ask from two people; this gathers DIFFERENT asks at one place, and a building is bigger than a grid rounding error.
supply_kinds_note: multi_taker and modifiers are per KIND, not per type. resupply is one request type spanning six crates: hammers come in three sizes and a FOB kit comes in one, and four of the six are jobs several drivers can run at once. The row stores the resolved value at submit.
multi_taker_note: multi_taker true means MANY people may accept the row: it stays on every board collecting takers instead of leaving on the first claim. False is the single-claimant path. Null on resupply only, where the chosen supply kind decides.
catalog_v5_note: v5. Outcome-first: a request names the effect wanted at a point, not the role that fills it. Retired: air_extract, air_move, anti_air_fire, anti_armor_fire, armor_support, close_air, fire_team, ground_extract, ground_move, overwatch, shell_mission, smoke_screen. Renamed: utility_medical->medical, utility_tactical->tactical, utility_recon->recon, utility_vehicle->vehicle. Every one needs a migration; stored type ids are never validated on read.
ttl_note: ttl_s is the wait for a TAKER and nothing else. A single-taker row stops ageing the moment somebody accepts it, because there is no time limit on doing the job. A multi_taker row keeps ageing while it collects people, or it would never clean itself up.
